source: The Agriculture Magazine ('សៀវភៅរបាយការណ៍កសិកម្ម'), issue 30, quarter 4 2010, article 'ពូជស្រូវសំខាន់ៗសម្រាប់ផលិតកម្មស្រូវ និងនាំអង្ករចេញ' (Important Rice Varieties for Rice Production and Export), citing the IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank and CARDI rice-variety descriptions in its reference list
text: The article's second group covers flood-tolerant, photoperiod-sensitive fragrant rice varieties, which flower on a fixed calendar date regardless of when they were sown and are prized for aroma and export/market value. Two are clearly identified by name and photo caption in the article: Phka Romdeng and Phka Romeat. A third fragrant variety is described in the same section (grown similarly, promoted through the same extension program) but its exact Khmer/English name was not clearly legible from the scanned magazine image and should be verified against the original print copy or CARDI's variety list before use. These fragrant varieties are characterized as longer-duration, photoperiod-sensitive types typically suited to rainfed lowland or flood-prone fields, valued for higher market price and export demand despite lower yield potential than the short-duration group.
